## What carries the design claim (identifiability)
"Design" is confounded with dataset (one dataset per design except sports), so we do **not** claim crowd-vs-expert in general. The design evidence is:
(i) **matched contrasts**, paired and within-graph: Arena battles, crowd vs each LLM judge (potsawee); MT-Bench pairs, expert vs GPT-4; uncertainty by resampling battles/questions jointly;
(ii) the several judges in potsawee as replicates of the LLM-judge design;
(iii) NBA seasons (regular season, ~70) as replicates of the sports design;
(iv) Arena-140k vs 55k, plus category/language/time slices of 140k, as replicates within crowd.
Claims are limited to the instances studied and the paper says so.

To our knowledge, among the sources we could consult: (1) a common scale for noise and intent (SE-unit fragility F, its ratio to the null, P_flip curves); (2) design-vs-statistics separation by matched contrasts and a parametric-bootstrap null; (3) search-vs-exact sandwich for fragility; (4) CI-separated ≠ robust, quantified per design as a curve; (5) a calibration, out of sample, of what predicts k*: held-out comparison of the regression rule, the same-graph null's k*, the rescaled first-order influence estimate, log z alone and the intercept (log z carries most of it; N, density and ties add little beyond the same-graph reference; k* is predicted to a factor of about 1.3 from one influence computation, without search). "Dropping a few votes changes the top model" is a replication-type observation inside (1), not the headline.

Starter item 8 (Huang et al. 2025) was **not read** (forbidden-paper rule); the two April-2026 BT-perturbation preprints are **not to be read**: not needed. Cite item 8 only as listed in the starter file; reproduction notes say it was not read.

## What would change the idea
- F/z matches the null and Real − Null ≈ 0: main finding "fragility is statistical: set by z and N, not by who judges", with the collapse and predictive rule as the deliverable.
- Real − Null > 0 in some designs: the finding is which misfit (position/length bias, draws, schedule) carries it, shown on the matched contrasts.
- Linear search far from exact in some design: the gap is part of the main finding.

cd /hutian/idea-wiki && python3 - <<'E'
s=open('Brief.md').read()
a=s.index("- H2 (design vs statistics)"); b=s.index("\n",a)
s=s[:a]+"- H2 (design vs statistics), restated in rev 8 after the positive control (`experiment-repo`#9): a design can matter for fragility through (a) the *margin* z (its SE, i.e. the clustering design effect = cluster-bootstrap SE / model SE) or (b) *misfit* that moves k\\* at fixed z. (a) is measured by the **SE ratio** and by the matched contrasts (same battles/pairs, different judges, joint resampling). (b) is gauged by Δ(log Q) = Real − Null on the same graph, **but the positive control shows Δ does not respond to any injected departure tried** (overdispersion, position bias, cycle, pair-specific deviation; |Δ| ≤ 0.04 while the SE ratio moves 0.82 → 2.26), so Δ ≈ 0 says only that real k\\* follows the same-graph null as the null follows itself (a statement about the margin), not that BT fits. H2 is therefore tested through the SE ratio and the matched contrasts, with Δ reported as a gauge of limited power."+s[b:]
s=s.replace("(2) design-vs-statistics separation by matched contrasts and a parametric-bootstrap null;","(2) design-vs-statistics separation by matched contrasts, the SE ratio (design effect) and a parametric-bootstrap null, with the positive control showing which of these instruments can see a departure (the SE ratio can, Δ(log Q) cannot);")
s=s.replace("k* is predicted to a factor of about 1.3 from one influence computation, without search).","flips are predicted to a factor of about 1.2 from one influence computation plus a median-bias rescale, whose constant is fitted on the other data sets; deletion to about 1.3 from the fitted rule or the null reference, which needs a search on null replicates; the rescaled first-order estimate is worse for deletion, RMSE 0.38).")
s=s.replace("- F/z matches the null and Real − Null ≈ 0: main finding","- F/z matches the null and Real − Null ≈ 0 (rev 8: this alone does not show BT fits, since Δ has no power against the departures tried; the SE ratio and matched contrasts carry the design claim): main finding")
s=s.replace("- Real − Null > 0 in some designs:","- Fragility differs by design mainly through the SE ratio (one found: MT-Bench human, question clustering, design effect 2.39): the finding is that design acts on the margin, not on k\\* at fixed z. If Real − Null > 0 in some designs:")
open('Brief.md','w').write(s)
E

shown.message:
I agreed with `story-repo`'s request in `idea-repo`#8, rewrote the Brief as rev 8 (pushed), and closed the issue. I also applied the idea-review precision point from #7 to the same revision.

- **H2:** a design can act on the margin z, measured by the SE ratio (cluster-bootstrap SE over model SE) and the matched contrasts. It can also act through misfit that moves k\* at fixed z.
- **Δ(log Q) as a gauge:** the positive control shows Δ does not respond to any departure tried, so Δ ≈ 0 only says real k\* follows the same-graph null. The Brief now reports it as a low-power gauge, and "Δ ≈ 0" is worded as a statement about the margin, not about BT fit.
- **What changes in the idea:** one design effect has been found so far, MT-Bench human with question clustering (design effect 2.39). The Brief now offers "design acts on the margin, not on k\* at fixed z" as the finding if that pattern holds. The lead (counts, null, noise vs adversary, survival) is unchanged.
- **Contribution (5):**
  - Flips are predicted to about 1.2 from one influence computation plus a median-bias rescale. The rescale constant is fitted on the other data sets.
  - Deletion is predicted to about 1.3 from the fitted rule or the null reference, which needs a search on null replicates.
  - The rescaled first-order estimate is worse for deletion, with RMSE 0.38.

I took the Δ and SE-ratio numbers from `story-repo`'s issue and did not recompute them. I commented on #7 about the contribution (5) wording and left that issue closed.
